scope: Theorem 9.1 (Lifting and Mixing) of the manuscript “Minimal models and Mori fibre spaces for generalized log canonical Q-pairs” (preprints/Minimal-models-and-Mori-fibre-spaces-for-generalized-log-canonical-Q-pairs-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 036 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 37e6d650c989c3fb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 45. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix positive integers d, r and a positive real number C. The following assertions hold. (1) Let P/Q be a regular extension with trdegC P ≤ d, having a projective Fano type generic model. Let σ, ψ be forms on P whose boundaries on this model are effective, with σ of index at most r. Suppose, on every nonzero divisorial valuation of P, that Aψ > 0, 0 ≤ Aσ ≤ CAψ. For every λ > 0 there is δ = δ(d, r, C, λ) > 0 with the following property. If u is a nonzero integral-valued divisorial valuation of Q and inf w|Q=u Aψ(w) < δ, then there is an integral-valued divisorial valuation v of P whose restriction is a positive multiple of u and for which Aψ(v) < λ. In relative dimension zero the regular extension is P = Q, and the same assertion holds. (2) Let P have a projective Fano type model over C of dimension at most d. Let σ, ψ, χ be forms with effective boundaries on that model, with σ of index at most r, and suppose Aψ > 0, 0 ≤ Aσ ≤ CAψ. Suppose in addition that, for some c > 0, Aχ(w) ≥ cAψ(w) whenever w ̸= 0 and Aσ(w) = 0. There is a rational number a ∈ (0, 1) depending only on d, r, C, c such that (1 − a)Aψ(w) + aAχ(w) > 0 for every nonzero divisorial w. All infima and homogeneous inequalities allow positive rational scalings of prime divisorial valuations. An integral-valued valuation is not required to be primitive.
